items.title: Preview seed fixture (rolling)
items.summary: Rolling, fully SYNTHETIC preview-database seed fixture baked from dev@6319f87b16f8 (migration head: 20261019120000_add_chat_message_trace_id). Preview environments restore fixture.dump.gz (custom-format, gzipped, platform schema only, including _prisma_migrations) BEFORE running a PR's own migrations, so schema changes run against populated tables. RESTORE: apply restore-preamble.sql to the target database first (it creates the platform schema and installs the vector + pg_trgm extensions into it, which pg_dump --schema=platform omits), then run 'gunzip -c fixture.dump.gz | pg_restore -d --no-owner' WITHOUT --exit-on-error (the dump's own CREATE SCHEMA collides benignly with the preamble's). SECURITY INVARIANT: this bake holds no cloud credentials and has no read path to any real database — it runs entirely against a throwaway Postgres container and contains only Faker-generated synthetic rows plus the already-public marketplace agent exports checked into autogpt_platform/backend/agents/. This asset is regenerated on every eligible dev push and weekly; treat it as disposable.

items.title: Show HN: Search for AI-agents and usefulness score
items.summary: We presented this project at innovationintelligencehackathon.com and today we are putting a url out for you to test and give us feedback. after talking to teams building agents that research companies to create outreach, we found few things that are very important to them. one of them is recency. When we prompted agents with outdated alert about companies, 4 out of 7 times, they came up with outdated insights, even when they had recent news in context. A bigger model didnt fix it. So we built search for ai-agents with usefulness score on top. So, when you search each page comes with score+price. this solve 3 problems; 1. token, SOTA agents read all pages to make sense of the useful ones 2. cost, when agents pay for pages they read, its is cost-effective to read only useful ones 3. quality, our score consider the task/query at hand and score useful pages, increasing quality of answers. we want to find out fast if we are really up to something here. we'd love to hear from you.
items.summary_html:
We presented this project at innovationintelligencehackathon.com and today we are putting a url out for you to test and give us feedback. after talking to teams building agents that research companies to create outreach, we found few things that are very important to them. one of them is recency. When we prompted agents with outdated alert about companies, 4 out of 7 times, they came up with outdated insights, even when they had recent news in context. A bigger model didnt fix it. So we built search for ai-agents with usefulness score on top. So, when you search each page comes with score+price.

this solve 3 problems;

1. token, SOTA agents read all pages to make sense of the useful ones

2. cost, when agents pay for pages they read, its is cost-effective to read only useful ones

3. quality, our score consider the task/query at hand and score useful pages, increasing quality of answers.

we want to find out fast if we are really up to something here. we'd love to hear from you.

items.title: Ask HN: What have you built privately with AI that you'd like to share?
items.summary: An idea has circulated that a lot of us are just privately building software for our own projects without sharing the build We could however share the ideas of what we're building so that other people could build sometime similar to fill their own needs or the ideas could be incorporated in to other projects A lot of random things come to mind for me, like I started (but for now abandoned) some kind of picture icon viewer by date on Linux desktop. A lot of smartphone file viewers display pics this way automatically and it lets you look at what pics you've accumulated day by day, but I didn't see this feature on different Linux file viewers (and it was apparently a requested feature others were looking for). So what have you built privately with AI that you might like to share ideas about? edit: alternatively, are there any things you'd like to see others create (and I suppose a comment about what holds you back from creating them)?
items.summary_html:
An idea has circulated that a lot of us are just privately building software for our own projects without sharing the build

We could however share the ideas of what we're building so that other people could build sometime similar to fill their own needs or the ideas could be incorporated in to other projects

A lot of random things come to mind for me, like I started (but for now abandoned) some kind of picture icon viewer by date on Linux desktop. A lot of smartphone file viewers display pics this way automatically and it lets you look at what pics you've accumulated day by day, but I didn't see this feature on different Linux file viewers (and it was apparently a requested feature others were looking for).

So what have you built privately with AI that you might like to share ideas about?

edit: alternatively, are there any things you'd like to see others create (and I suppose a comment about what holds you back from creating them)?
